evaluationTargets.title: Activation of revised customer refund-authority policy across support operations
evaluationTargets.context: A policy change expands frontline agent refund authority to reduce escalation delays, taking effect across all support teams at once.
evaluationTargets.operationalImpact: Incorrect refunds could cause financial leakage, while over-strict handling could wrongly deny valid customer claims.

qualityIntents.statement: Expanded refund authority must not enable refunds above the approved financial limit without secondary approval.
qualityIntents.lossBoundary: Refunds must not exceed the policy financial limit without secondary approval.

qualityIntents.statement: Customers with valid refund claims must not be wrongly denied because of the policy change.
qualityIntents.lossBoundary: Valid refund claims must not be denied due to policy misconfiguration.

qualityIntents.statement: The policy change must be reversible if leakage or complaints exceed containment thresholds.
qualityIntents.lossBoundary: An unsafe policy state must not persist without a demonstrated reversal path.

qualityAspects.name: functional suitability
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether the target performs the intended behavior or service outcome.
discoveryQuestions: What must work for the target to be acceptable?
possibleLossBoundaries: Required behavior must not fail on protected cases.
antiPatterns: Treating feature presence as proof that the intended outcome is protected.

qualityAspects.name: business fit
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether the target supports the business purpose without creating unacceptable tradeoffs.
discoveryQuestions: Which business outcome would be harmed even if the mechanism works?
possibleLossBoundaries: The business process must not create unacceptable stakeholder harm.
antiPatterns: Treating revenue or throughput as quality itself.

qualityAspects.name: usability
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether intended users can complete the work correctly and efficiently.
discoveryQuestions: What would a trained but non-expert user misunderstand or miss?
possibleLossBoundaries: Users must not be led into materially incorrect action by the target.
antiPatterns: Treating attractive layout as evidence of usable operation.

qualityAspects.name: ux design
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether the end-to-end experience preserves comprehension, trust, and appropriate user control.
discoveryQuestions: Where could the experience create false confidence or hide an important boundary?
possibleLossBoundaries: The experience must not obscure a decision consequence that users must understand.
antiPatterns: Treating visual polish as proof that the experience is safe or understandable.

qualityAspects.name: accessibility
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether affected users can access and operate the target without exclusion.
discoveryQuestions: Who cannot perceive, understand, navigate, or act on this target?
possibleLossBoundaries: Eligible users must not be excluded from critical action or information.
antiPatterns: Treating accessibility as optional decoration after release.

qualityAspects.name: performance efficiency
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether response time, effort, or resource use stays within acceptable boundaries.
discoveryQuestions: What delay or resource use would make the target unacceptable?
possibleLossBoundaries: Critical work must not exceed the delay or effort tolerance.
antiPatterns: Treating average speed as proof that critical cases are protected.

qualityAspects.name: scalability
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether the target still works when volume, complexity, or demand changes.
discoveryQuestions: What breaks first if volume doubles?
possibleLossBoundaries: Expected growth must not make the protected process unsafe or unusable.
antiPatterns: Assuming today's low volume proves tomorrow's adequacy.

qualityAspects.name: availability
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether the target is reachable or usable when stakeholders need it.
discoveryQuestions: When must this be available, and what outage is unacceptable?
possibleLossBoundaries: Critical users must not lose access during protected operating windows.
antiPatterns: Treating uptime percentage alone as quality.

qualityAspects.name: reliability
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether the target behaves consistently under expected conditions.
discoveryQuestions: Which repeated use would expose inconsistency or drift?
possibleLossBoundaries: Repeated protected actions must not produce materially inconsistent outcomes.
antiPatterns: Treating one successful run as reliability proof.

qualityAspects.name: recoverability
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether the organization can restore a safe state after failure.
discoveryQuestions: How do we return to a known safe state if this goes wrong?
possibleLossBoundaries: An unsafe state must not persist without a demonstrated recovery path.
antiPatterns: Treating a written rollback plan as proof without rehearsal when risk is high.

qualityAspects.name: security
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether authority, confidentiality, integrity, or trust boundaries are protected.
discoveryQuestions: What authority or data boundary could be crossed?
possibleLossBoundaries: Unauthorized parties must not gain access or authority.
antiPatterns: Treating authentication presence as proof that authorization risk is controlled.

qualityAspects.name: privacy
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether personal or sensitive information is used, exposed, retained, or inferred acceptably.
discoveryQuestions: What sensitive information could be exposed or used beyond expectation?
possibleLossBoundaries: Sensitive information must not be exposed or retained beyond approved purpose.
antiPatterns: Treating legal consent text as proof that actual data handling is acceptable.

qualityAspects.name: data quality
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether data remains accurate, complete, timely, and interpretable enough for decisions.
discoveryQuestions: Which decision fails if this data is wrong, stale, or incomplete?
possibleLossBoundaries: Decisions must not rely on materially incorrect or stale data.
antiPatterns: Treating data existence as proof that data is fit for use.

qualityAspects.name: operational quality
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether the target can be operated, monitored, and handed off safely.
discoveryQuestions: Who operates this, and what would they need during an abnormal state?
possibleLossBoundaries: Operators must not be left unable to detect or contain harmful states.
antiPatterns: Treating launch completion as proof of operational readiness.

qualityAspects.name: maintainability
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether future maintainers can understand, diagnose, and preserve the target.
discoveryQuestions: What would a future maintainer be unable to understand or safely change?
possibleLossBoundaries: Future maintenance must not require hidden expert-only knowledge for protected work.
antiPatterns: Treating low defect count as proof of maintainability.

qualityAspects.name: changeability
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether the target can adapt to expected change without disproportionate risk.
discoveryQuestions: Which likely change would be expensive or risky to make?
possibleLossBoundaries: Expected changes must not require unsafe or opaque workarounds.
antiPatterns: Treating current correctness as proof of future adaptability.

qualityAspects.name: auditability
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether decisions, evidence, and authority can be reconstructed later.
discoveryQuestions: Can an auditor reconstruct why this was accepted?
possibleLossBoundaries: Governed decisions must not become impossible to reconstruct.
antiPatterns: Treating a passed verifier as proof of semantic correctness.

qualityAspects.name: compliance
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether external obligations, policies, or standards impose quality boundaries.
discoveryQuestions: Which rule, contract, or policy would be violated if this passes?
possibleLossBoundaries: The target must not violate governing obligations.
antiPatterns: Treating generic policy acknowledgement as evidence of compliance.

qualityAspects.name: safety
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether people, equipment, environment, or critical operations could be harmed.
discoveryQuestions: What physical, operational, or severe harm could this enable?
possibleLossBoundaries: The target must not enable unacceptable safety exposure.
antiPatterns: Treating lack of past incidents as proof of safety.

qualityAspects.name: cost efficiency
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether cost, effort, or waste becomes unacceptable relative to value.
discoveryQuestions: What cost or rework would make this unacceptable?
possibleLossBoundaries: The target must not impose disproportionate avoidable cost on stakeholders.
antiPatterns: Treating low implementation cost as proof of quality.

qualityAspects.name: customer impact
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether customers experience loss, unfairness, confusion, or unmet expectations.
discoveryQuestions: Which customer would be harmed or treated unfairly if this passes?
possibleLossBoundaries: Customers must not absorb unacceptable avoidable harm.
antiPatterns: Treating internal process completion as proof of customer acceptability.

qualityAspects.name: brand trust
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether the target could damage trust, credibility, or perceived fairness.
discoveryQuestions: What would make stakeholders lose trust even if the action is technically allowed?
possibleLossBoundaries: The organization must not create unjustifiable trust loss.
antiPatterns: Treating legal permissibility as proof of trust acceptability.

qualityAspects.name: organizational operability
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether the organization can staff, train, govern, and sustain the target.
discoveryQuestions: What depends on expert-only knowledge or unclear ownership?
possibleLossBoundaries: The organization must not depend on hidden knowledge for governed operation.
antiPatterns: Treating a veteran's approval as automatically reproducible organizational knowledge.

evaluationPerspectives.rationale: The activation is an all-at-once operational change that needs an explicit Go, Conditional Go, No-Go, or Pending decision.
Whether the refund-limit control and claim handling behave as intended under the new authority.
Whether previously valid claims continue to be approved after the change.
Whether reversal, monitoring, and post-activation impact are covered.
The aspect taxonomy was used as an exploration map to avoid blind spots; aspect presence is not treated as proof that quality was achieved.

evidenceTypeVocabulary.purpose: Record sampled human or AI-assisted review findings that may reveal escapes or regressions.
antiPatterns: Treating sample size or review count as quality itself.

evidenceTypeVocabulary.purpose: Record direct control behavior under representative protected scenarios.
antiPatterns: Treating one passing control test as proof that all operating contexts are safe.

evidenceTypeVocabulary.purpose: Record representative checks that previously valid outcomes still remain valid.
antiPatterns: Treating regression case count as quality itself.

evidenceTypeVocabulary.purpose: Record evidence that a risky change can return to a known safe state.
antiPatterns: Treating a written rollback plan as rehearsal evidence.

evidenceTypeVocabulary.purpose: Record monitoring configuration before real operating observations are available.
antiPatterns: Treating configured monitoring as proof that the system behaved safely in production.

evidenceItems.finding: In a re-adjudication sample of 120 historical refund cases under the new policy, 3 would exceed the financial limit without secondary approval.
evidenceItems.retention: Retained in the quality evidence store for 24 months.

evidenceItems.finding: A control test attempted 40 over-limit refunds; the secondary-approval step blocked all 40 before completion.
evidenceItems.retention: Retained with the release evidence bundle for 24 months.

evidenceItems.finding: A regression sample of 60 previously approved valid claims were all still approved under the new policy.
A reversal rehearsal restored the prior policy configuration in 12 minutes with no residual refund-authority state.
Refund-leakage and complaint-rate monitoring is configured with alert thresholds, but has not yet been observed under real activation load.
evidenceItems.retention: Configuration retained; observations to follow after activation.

quantitativeEvidenceRecords.metricName: over-limit refund escape count in sample
quantitativeEvidenceRecords.measurementMethod: Manual re-adjudication of 120 sampled historical refund cases under the new policy.
quantitativeEvidenceRecords.interpretationRule: More than zero over-limit escapes means the secondary-approval control must demonstrably block them before a full Go.
quantitativeEvidenceRecords.knownLimitation: A 120-case sample may miss rare edge cases; the count is a signal, not a quality score.

quantitativeEvidenceRecords.measurementMethod: Control test over 40 attempted over-limit refunds; blocked divided by attempted.
quantitativeEvidenceRecords.interpretationRule: A block rate below 1.0 on over-limit refunds is a No-Go for the financial-limit boundary; 1.0 supports but does not by itself prove protection.
quantitativeEvidenceRecords.knownLimitation: The test used simulated over-limit refunds, not live traffic.

quantitativeEvidenceRecords.measurementMethod: Regression sample of 60 previously approved valid claims re-evaluated under the new policy.
quantitativeEvidenceRecords.interpretationRule: A retention rate below 1.0 indicates valid claims are being wrongly denied and downgrades the claim-fairness verdict.
quantitativeEvidenceRecords.knownLimitation: Sample cannot cover every claim category.

quantitativeEvidenceRecords.measurementMethod: Timed reversal rehearsal from decision to restored prior configuration.
quantitativeEvidenceRecords.interpretationRule: Reversal must complete within the 30-minute containment target; longer reversal weakens the reversibility intent.
quantitativeEvidenceRecords.knownLimitation: Rehearsal conditions may be calmer than a real incident.

qualityGateRules.title: Financial-limit boundary must be control-protected before Go.
blockingConditions: No-Go if the over-limit control block rate is below 1.0.
At most Conditional Go while any sampled over-limit escape remains without a compensating control.

qualityGateRules.title: Reversibility must be demonstrated for high-severity policy changes.
blockingConditions: No-Go if no reversal evidence exists.
At most Conditional Go while monitoring has not been observed under real load.

qualityGateRules.title: Valid-claim regression must hold.
blockingConditions: At most Conditional Go if the valid-claim retention rate is below 1.0.

intentVerdicts.residualRisk: Three sampled cases could exceed the limit if the secondary-approval step is bypassed.
Claim categories outside the sample remain unverified.
Monitoring is configured but not yet observed under real activation load.

residualRisks: Over-limit refunds could still occur if agents bypass secondary approval.
Leakage and complaint monitoring has not been observed under real load.

conditions.condition: The secondary-approval step must remain mandatory and non-bypassable for any refund above the financial limit.
conditions.monitoring: Daily audit of over-limit refunds for the first 30 days after activation.

conditions.condition: Leakage and complaint dashboards must be actively watched with alert thresholds during the containment window.
conditions.monitoring: Alert when leakage exceeds baseline or complaints rise more than 20 percent week over week.

qualityGateDecisions.rollbackPlan: Revert to the prior refund-authority policy within 30 minutes using the rehearsed reversal procedure recorded in EVD-QG-004.
qualityGateDecisions.monitoringPlan: Track refund leakage amount, over-limit escape count, and complaint volume across 7-day and 30-day windows.
qualityGateDecisions.customerImpactPlan: Notify affected customers and reprocess any wrongly denied valid claims within five business days.

qualityReports.title: Refund authority activation quality report
qualityReports.reportPurpose: Summarize the quality-gate decision for accountable release review without treating the summary score as quality itself.
qualityReports.summary: The target is a Conditional Go because each protected intent has evidence-backed verdicts, while over-limit leakage and unobserved live monitoring remain residual risks.

reportedScores.label: Gate confidence summary
reportedScores.calculationNote: This score reports the gate decision confidence, which is reproduced from intent verdict confidence values and the referenced confidence policy.

sections.heading: Release verdict
sections.narrative: The Conditional Go depends on mandatory secondary approval, active leakage monitoring, and a rehearsed rollback path.

limitations: The report is a decomposable summary of referenced verdicts and evidence; it does not create new semantic proof.
The score must not be interpreted independently from its cited verdict and evidence chain.
antiPatterns: Reporting a quality score that cannot be traced back to gate verdicts and evidence.
Treating report publication as quality approval.

incidents.description: Two over-limit refunds were issued when an agent bypassed the secondary-approval step during a high-volume period.

postReleaseReviews.summary: The financial-limit boundary was breached twice because secondary approval was bypassable under load, confirming the residual risk recorded at the gate.

improvementActions.title: Make secondary approval non-bypassable for over-limit refunds
improvementActions.correctiveAction: Reconfigure the refund workflow so over-limit refunds cannot be submitted without a completed secondary approval, and add a weekly over-limit audit.
improvementActions.effectMeasurement: Over-limit escape count in the 30-day window after the fix, compared with the first 7-day window.

governanceTriggers.reason: The sampled over-limit escapes conflict with the control-test block rate, so the financial-limit protection needs accountable confirmation before the conditions are removed.

governanceEvents.decisionRationale: Activation may proceed as a Conditional Go because the over-limit control blocks simulated breaches, provided secondary approval stays mandatory and leakage is monitored during the containment window.

checks: quantitative records carry unit, method, and interpretation rule and stay evidence-only
gate verdict confidence reproducibility from evidence inputs and confidence policy
release decision completeness (rollback, monitoring, approval owner, residual risk, conditions)
high-severity boundaries are not supported only by low-independence evidence without governance
post-release high-severity incidents link to improvement actions
governance triggers on low confidence, conflict, or weak evidence
doesNotClaim: the organization chose the right quality perspectives
the metrics prove quality by themselves
a Go or Conditional Go decision is semantically correct without accountable review

evaluationTimingRules.title: Pre-release boundary evidence timing
triggerConditions: Gate decision includes a high-severity loss boundary.
Target changes operating authority or financial exposure.
evaluationTimingRules.latestAllowedStage: before Go or Conditional Go is recorded
antiPatterns: Approving release first and treating later evidence collection as equivalent.
Using planned review count as proof that boundary evidence exists.

evaluationTimingRules.title: Continuous post-activation monitoring timing
triggerConditions: The target remains active after the release gate decision.
Operational harm can emerge after activation through volume or exception drift.
evaluationTimingRules.latestAllowedStage: active monitoring window after policy activation
antiPatterns: Treating release approval as the end of quality evaluation.
Counting monitoring events without linking them to loss boundaries.

evaluationTimingDecisions.decisionRationale: The gate protects high-severity financial and reversibility boundaries, so control and rollback evidence must exist before Conditional Go is recorded.
Customer-denial and rollback risks can emerge after activation, so monitoring remains active after the gate decision.

evidenceRetentionPolicies.title: Release evidence retention policy
evidenceRetentionPolicies.retentionPeriod: 24 months after policy activation or until superseded by governance decision
evidenceRetentionPolicies.disposalRule: Dispose only after retention period expires and no governance trigger, audit request, or post-release review remains open.
antiPatterns: Keeping only summary counts while discarding evidence artifacts.
Treating retention duration as quality itself.

evidenceRetentionPolicies.title: Operational monitoring evidence retention policy
evidenceRetentionPolicies.disposalRule: Archive configuration and observation references after the monitoring window unless an incident or governance trigger requires extended retention.
antiPatterns: Discarding monitoring configuration before post-release review.
Counting monitoring events without retaining reconstructable evidence.
